items.streamTitle: Competitive rewards produced withdrawal and overinvestment in a 200-agent synthetic society
items.streamSummary: In 200 LLM agents across 50 rounds, low prizes yielded withdrawal while high rewards yielded modeled overcompetition. Widening eligibility changed collective cost and selection. These are synthetic dynamics, not human findings.
items.attribution: Zhao et al. — arXiv preprint (LLM-agent incentive simulation)

items.streamTitle: UNIDIR mapped 146 arms-related information disorders, mostly false claims about weapons flows
items.streamSummary: UNIDIR reviewed 146 conventional-arms information-disorder incidents from 2015–25; three quarters concerned arms flows, often using recycled media. Diplomatic and security effects are plausible but not quantified causally.
items.attribution: Sarah Grand-Clément — UNIDIR (original 40-page incident analysis, October 29)

items.streamTitle: VR eye-and-hand tracking measured distraction costs; richer scenes did not amplify capture
items.streamSummary: A 54-person VR study measured reliable distraction costs in gaze and reaching. More complex scenes increased some overall demands without significantly increasing capture effects, offering a reproducible measurement method rather than evidence of training benefits.
items.attribution: Gurr, Moher, Egbert and Erb — Behavior Research Methods (VR attention experiment)

items.streamTitle: Dishonest AI peer norms increased human misreporting, without a significant AI-versus-human difference
items.streamSummary: Two randomized die-reporting experiments (N=640) found dishonest peer cues increased misreporting; differences between AI and human peers were not significant. Effects were not monotonic with additional dishonest peers.
items.attribution: Shuning Zhang et al. — arXiv preprint (randomized behavioral experiments)

items.streamTitle: Adversarial AI comments reduced news discernment; warnings only partly reversed the effect
items.streamSummary: Two preregistered experiments (N=331) found adversarial AI comments and replies impaired news-veracity judgment. Warnings and detector cues partially helped, especially for top-level comments, but actual sharing was not observed.
items.attribution: Lu, Lim and Yin — CHI 2026 (preregistered randomized experiments)

items.streamTitle: Generative road-choice inference found no single rule across 62 Roman routes
items.streamSummary: A hierarchical generative model fit to 62 Roman roads found heterogeneous terrain-versus-directness trade-offs. The inferred motivations are model interpretations; transfer to present-day decision modeling remains untested.
items.attribution: Lewis and Crema — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (generative historical decision modeling)

items.streamTitle: Graphika traced renewed Spamouflage-linked election personas and mostly closed amplification
items.streamSummary: Graphika documented three Spamouflage-linked activity sets using voter personas, repurposed accounts and mostly in-network amplification. Attribution and audience reach are bounded; no voter effect was measured.
items.attribution: Graphika Research Team — The #Americans: Season 2 (original network investigation, October 30)

items.streamTitle: AI confidence and literacy correlated with acceptance and lower anxiety in students
items.streamSummary: A 622-student Turkish survey linked AI confidence and literacy to acceptance, and acceptance to lower anxiety. The reported mediated pathways are correlational, not evidence that literacy training caused adoption.
items.attribution: İşbulan et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (cross-sectional survey)

items.streamTitle: Imagined contact with moral exemplars shifted adolescents’ reported prosocial tendencies
items.streamSummary: A six-class, 207-student guided-imagery experiment linked imagined contact with positive moral exemplars to higher self-reported prosociality. The outcome was not actual helping, and statistical mediation did not prove a mechanism.
items.attribution: Li and Yang — Scientific Reports (class-based guided-imagery experiment)

items.streamTitle: Agent workload benchmark exposed large drops from isolated to concurrent task delivery
items.streamSummary: AOS-Bench compared five agent configurations on isolated versus shared workloads and found heavy-load success fell 13–23 points. Intake and concurrency policy mattered; agent self-reported completion was not the scoring criterion.
items.attribution: Zhu et al. — arXiv preprint (AOS-Bench verified agent evaluation)

items.streamTitle: LLM collectives showed exaggerated recommendation herding and unstable cascades
items.streamSummary: A Music Lab-style experiment found LLM-agent populations herded strongly when shown popularity counts, with more extreme and less self-correcting cascades than human comparators. It is AI-agent evidence, not human-field validation.
items.attribution: Hashemi et al. — arXiv preprint (LLM-agent social-influence simulations)

items.streamTitle: Coordinated fake-local-news sites reached chatbot citations in election queries
items.streamSummary: VisionHeight documented 37 coordinated election-information sites designed for machine retrieval; NPR later observed their citations in 19 ChatGPT responses. The operator and effects on voters remain unknown.
items.attribution: VisionHeight — VH-2026-035 original investigation (October 7), with NPR follow-up (October 30)

items.streamTitle: New revelations reshaped remembered opinions of creators more than their work
items.streamSummary: Five preregistered experiments found that negative revelations changed recollections of liking an artist more than recollections of liking the art. The result concerns retrospective judgments, not verified changes in past experience.
items.attribution: Shin, Rozin and Zauberman — Journal of Experimental Social Psychology (five preregistered experiments)

items.streamTitle: OpenEye measured cross-headset gaze tracking with a reproducible calibration toolkit
items.streamSummary: An open-source external eye-tracking toolkit improved Quest 3 gaze error from 2.281° to 1.727° and was tested on two additional headsets. Accuracy was measured in controlled tasks, not naturalistic attention studies.
items.attribution: Park, Han and Oakley — Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction (cross-device toolkit evaluation)

items.streamTitle: Army's Project Convergence tested integrated C2 while targeting cognitive-load reductions
items.streamSummary: Army officials described a large July command-and-control experiment reported October 30, including 9,700 soldiers and over 90 technologies. Faster decisions and lower cognitive load were objectives, not published results.
items.attribution: Nina Borgeson — U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (official report)

items.streamTitle: New framework distinguishes AI-assisted task success from durable human learning
items.streamSummary: A 2026 Perspective introduces the SYNC model separating immediate human–AI performance from durable learning and metacognitive engagement. Its proposed pitfalls and scaffolds are conceptual, not validated experimental effects.
items.attribution: Fan et al. — Communications Psychology (theoretical Perspective)

items.streamTitle: Autonomous research agent completed five reproducible papers, with AI-only quality review
items.streamSummary: Five consecutive autonomous coding-agent runs produced papers whose analyses could be rerun, with cross-model critique. Outcomes depended strongly on agenda wording, and positive quality ratings came from AI judges rather than human reviewers.
items.attribution: Ko Fujimura — arXiv preprint (autonomous research-agent case series)

items.streamTitle: Research-agent team halted a plausible experiment after uncovering measurement drift
items.streamSummary: A multi-role AI laboratory found drifting reference measurements, rejected an initially positive experimental interpretation, and retested a diamond-spin prediction. One bounded demonstration does not establish general autonomous scientific reliability.
items.attribution: Mansouri, Kimura, Koga and Arai — arXiv preprint (experimental AI research workflow)

items.streamTitle: Strong violations of memory-based predictions recruited attention and control
items.streamSummary: Two memory experiments involving 101 adults found strong prediction violations recruited greater attention-, arousal-, and control-related signals, with frontal theta related to learning. Neural mediation and field transfer remain unproven.
items.attribution: Xue, Jokhani, Norcia and Wagner — eLife (EEG/pupillometry experiments)

items.streamTitle: Crisis-resilience review found competing definitions and measurement gaps
items.streamSummary: A NATO-accredited centre's 48-page review maps civilian resilience across individuals, communities, and nations while identifying conceptual and measurement gaps. It supplies a research agenda, not a validated crisis forecast.
items.attribution: Lindgren, Svenonius, Palmer and Bertolin — NATO Strategic Communications Centre of Excellence (literature review)

items.streamTitle: Algebraic activation improved uncertainty and convergence in fuzzy grey cognitive maps
items.streamSummary: A Neurocomputing comparison found Elliot-family activation functions reduced uncertainty measures and computation in tested fuzzy grey cognitive maps. Stable simulations do not establish valid behavioral causal predictions.
items.attribution: Salmeron and Pueyo — Neurocomputing (mathematical and simulation study)

items.streamTitle: LLM-society surrogate tests separated individual accuracy from collective fidelity
items.streamSummary: Analysis of 9,455 LLM-agent trajectories found neighbor context improved one-step prediction, while collective forecasts and history benefits were conditional and partly nonreplicated. Human-group validity was not tested.
items.attribution: Igor Itkin — arXiv preprint (LLM-agent surrogate-model evaluation)

items.streamTitle: More immersive 360-degree VR did not outperform ordinary video for decision transfer
items.streamSummary: A small randomized four-week sports-training study found ordinary 2D video beat 360VR on field decision transfer. Immersion did not guarantee improved performance; non-sport transfer remains untested.
items.attribution: Hoyne et al. — Psychological Research (randomized training experiment)

items.streamTitle: Inductive headline training improved discernment; badges weakened the benefit
items.streamSummary: Three preregistered experiments (N=1,135) found feedback-based headline classification could improve true/false discernment. Adding badges weakened the effect; reversing the difficulty sequence restored stronger support. Actual sharing was not tested.
items.attribution: Modirrousta-Galian et al. — Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied (preregistered experiments)
